title: A basket of snakes
takeaway: Leaders without a conscience will sell anything, even their own people.
scene: A short, bitter four-line poem about corrupt leaders, printed straight after the Bhutto poem.

original: ایہہ تے لیڈر نرے مداری نیں
زہری سپاں دی اک پٹاری نیں
transliteration: Eh te leader nire madaari nain
Zehri sappaan di ik pitaari nain
translation: These leaders are nothing but street performers;
they're a basket of poisonous snakes.
couplets.story: He says the leaders are like street magicians putting on a show. Behind the show, they're a basket of poisonous snakes.

original: بے ضمیرے ایہہ قوم نوں پئے ویچن
بے حیائی دے ایہہ بیوپاری نیں
transliteration: Be-zameere eh qaum nu pae vechan
translation: Without a conscience, they're selling off the nation;
couplets.story: They have no conscience, and they're selling out the country. Shamelessness is their business.

why: Sharp and short. It shows how frustrated ordinary people felt with corrupt politicians.
prompt: What qualities do you think a good leader must have?
notes: A 'madaari' is a street performer, often a snake-charmer, which links to the 'basket of snakes' in the next line.
